entries.text: There’s a book entitled “Galar: A History.”\nDo you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_01_00

entries.text: Galar: A History
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_01_title

entries.text:
We made for the town of Stow-on-Side, which
sits tucked away in the mountains, to study an
ancient mural painted upon a wall of rock.
But our plans—and the mural itself—were
shattered by an attack from a Copperajah!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_01_01

entries.text:
Yet behind the mural, what should we find but a
pair of Pokémon statues—one bearing a sword,
the other a shield! These statues, older than any
artifact we’d yet discovered, called into question
everything we knew about the legendary hero.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_01_02

entries.text: There’s a book entitled “Festivals of Paldea.”\nDo you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_02_00

entries.text: Festivals of Paldea
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_02_title

entries.text:
The Paldean town of Cortondo, widely known for
its olive production, is also home to the peculiar
Olive Harvest Festival. Participants try to usher in
a plentiful olive harvest by rolling large balls that
resemble olives into a goal.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_02_01

entries.text:
It’s said that the more olive balls are rolled to the
goal, the more abundant next year’s crop will be.
All comers, including tourists, are welcome to
join the Olive Roll—so, reader, do give it a try
yourself if you’re in town for the festival!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_02_02

entries.text: There’s a book entitled “Appreciating Sunflora.”\nDo you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_03_00

entries.text: Appreciating Sunflora
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_03_title

entries.text:
In Artazon, a town alive with flowers and artwork,
there is a special and abiding love for the Sun
Pokémon Sunflora, whose sunny, floral figure and
bright smile never fail to warm the heart.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_03_01

entries.text:
Denizens of Artazon have long revered nature—
the subject of much art made in the town—and
the nurturing sun. Sunflora embodies qualities of
both, which is why the town has a tradition of
gathering and caring for these Pokémon.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_03_02

entries.text: There’s a book entitled “How to Become a\nChampion.” Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_05_00

entries.text: How to Become a Champion
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_05_title

entries.text:
For Pokémon Trainers who are out to grow
stronger and wiser, there’s no higher calling than
becoming a Champion! To reach that lofty rank,
you must pass a test administered at Paldea’s
official Pokémon League headquarters.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_05_01

entries.text:
In Paldea, anyone—and in fact, any number of
people—can become a Champion, regardless of
factors like age. That means you can too, as long
as you’ve got the strength and the wisdom to set
a leaderly example for your fellow Trainers!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_05_02

entries.text:
Your path to becoming a Champion lies in the
Pokémon Gyms throughout Paldea. Once you’ve
defeated the eight Gym Leaders in battle and
earned their Gym Badges, we look forward to
your knock on the Pokémon League’s door.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_05_03

entries.text: There’s a magazine entitled “Paldean Sports\nMonthly.” Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_06_00

entries.text: Paldean Sports Monthly
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_06_title

entries.text:
The Sub-zero Shredder has done it again! The
world’s second-ranked snowboarder put on a
clinic at the Montenevera Cup, claiming his sixth
straight win in Paldea’s major competitions. No
one’s been able to snatch that crown yet!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_06_01

entries.text:
“If you think you’ve got what it takes, come take
me on!” this ice-cold athlete declared from the
winners’ podium, and you could just feel his rivals
steel their resolve! We’ll see how things unfold
in two weeks at the Glaseado Mountain Cup!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_06_02

entries.text: There’s a magazine entitled “Sweet Truth!”\nDo you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_08_00

entries.text: Sweet Truth!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_08_title

entries.text:
This tasty pastry wonder is undergoing a
popularity sugar rush that’s got lines out the
door all day long! It’s Patisserie Soapberry,
located in Cortondo—olive central—at the foot
of a very large tree!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_08_01

entries.text:
At the heart of it all is Katy, the proprietor, who
inherited the shop from family and keeps its
ovens hard at work! Soapberry’s Bug-type
Pokémon theme is on full display in its pastry
lineup—they’re a treat to see and to eat!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_08_02

entries.text: There’s a magazine entitled “The Musician’s\nRegister.” Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_09_00

entries.text: The Musician’s Register
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_09_title

entries.text:
Four decades into her career, Ryme—the “MC of
RIP,” whose flows are said to bring the dead to
their feet—maintains her huge following and her
rap legend status. The theme of death pervades
her work—and not just because her bars slay.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_09_01

entries.text:
When Ryme was in her teens, her dear Puppy
Pokémon passed away, and she poured her grief
into a song. When she sang it, her partner came
back to her as a ghost Pokémon. In that moment,
the rapper we know today was born.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_09_02

entries.text: There’s a magazine entitled “Art: The Scenic\nRoute.” Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_10_00

entries.text: Art: The Scenic Route
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_10_title

entries.text:
This month, we’re taking the scenic route over
to Artazon to see Surrendering Sunflora by
Brassius, the Verdant Virtuoso. This humble
columnist wonders if ever a work has so aptly
captured ennui and languor as this installation.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_10_01

entries.text:
The sculptures are every bit as surreal as the title,
prompting great minds to debate just what has
sent these Sunflora into a state of surrender. But
though the meaning may elude us, the reader is
urged to visit Artazon and see for themselves.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_10_02

entries.text: There’s a book entitled “Status Conditions and\nCatching Pokémon.” Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_12_00

entries.text: Status Conditions and Catching Pokémon
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_12_title

entries.text:
Dealing damage to a wild Pokémon makes it
easier to catch in a Poké Ball, and inflicting
status conditions on the Pokémon can make it
easier still.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_12_01

entries.text:
Certain status conditions will provide even better
odds of a successful catch than others. Putting a
Pokémon to sleep or freezing it, for example,
may yield better results than inflicting poison,
paralysis, or a burn.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_12_02

entries.text: There’s a book entitled “Types and Moves I.”\nDo you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_13_00

entries.text: Types and Moves I
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_13_title

entries.text:
You may be familiar with Pokémon that are
Grass, Fire, or Water type. There are eighteen
such types in all, and every Pokémon species has
at least one type—some have two.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_13_01

entries.text:
When Pokémon use a move that is the same type
as they are, that move’s power is increased by
50 percent. For Pokémon that have two types,
moves of either type will receive this increase.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_13_02

entries.text: There’s a book entitled “Types and Moves II.”\nDo you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_14_00

entries.text: Types and Moves II
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_14_title

entries.text:
When Pokémon Terastallize, their type becomes
their [VAR 0xFF00(0006)]Tera Type[VAR 0xFF00(0000)]. That means moves of their Tera
Type will have their power increased. Moves of
the Pokémon’s original type will keep their usual
power increase as well.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_14_01

entries.text:
For example, if a Pikachu—which is innately
Electric type—has Steel as its Tera Type, then
upon Terastallizing it would receive boosts in
power for both the Steel-type move Iron Tail
and the Electric-type move Thunderbolt.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_14_02

entries.text: There’s a book entitled “Pokémon Natures.”\nDo you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_15_00

entries.text: Pokémon Natures
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_15_title

entries.text:
Individual Pokémon have different Natures, much
as people do. You may be able to get an idea of
your Pokémon’s Natures if you watch how they
behave on picnics—whether they run around a
lot or nap a lot, for example.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_15_01

entries.text:
Pokémon’s Natures influence their stats to a
degree. For example, Pokémon with Adamant
Natures tend to have their Attack stat grow
stronger than it would otherwise, while their
Sp. Atk stat may suffer.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_15_02

entries.text: There’s a book entitled “Fine Foods from Far\nAway.” Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_16_00

entries.text: Fine Foods from Far Away
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_16_title

entries.text:
Have you chanced upon Pewter Crunchies, the
fabled signature dish of the Kanto region’s
Pewter City? These snacks’ rugged, browned
appearance makes them almost rock-like at
first glance.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_16_01

entries.text:
Indeed, Pewter Crunchies were inspired by the
Rock-type Pokémon for which the Pewter Gym is
renowned. Unfortunately, their forbiddingly
tough appearance and surprisingly thin flavor
have kept them from attaining true popularity.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_16_02

entries.text: There’s a book entitled “Charcadet’s\nAdventures.” Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_17_00

entries.text: Charcadet’s Adventures
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_17_title

entries.text:
Charcadet, the Fire Child Pokémon, may have
been little, but did that stop it from being a
mighty hero? Not one bit! When a mean Gengar
came along to play tricks and scare people,
Charcadet stood tall! “Raaah! Hi-YAH!” it cried!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_17_01

entries.text:
But soon, brave little Charcadet got bound up
tight in Gengar’s looong tongue! How could the
Fire Child Pokémon get out of this mess?
Just as things started to grow hazy before
Charcadet’s eyes, the sound of a voice came...
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_17_02

entries.text:
“Two paths lie before you, young Charcadet,”
it said. “Choose between these two sets of armor
and assume a new form so you can defeat
Gengar!” And sure enough, two sets of armor
appeared before Charcadet... (To be continued)
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_17_03

entries.text: There’s a book entitled “Of People and\nPokémon.” Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_18_00

entries.text: Of People and Pokémon
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_18_title

entries.text:
Far in the past, humankind and Pokémon lived
in mutual fear of one another. But some humans
who loved and appreciated Pokémon made an
effort to bridge this divide, and gradually, the
two sides grew closer and found harmony.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_book_18_01

entries.text: Occulture
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_title_01

entries.text: An article caught your eye...
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_system_01

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #09\nGreat Tusk: A Living Relic of the Dinosaur Era?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_01_02a

entries.text:
In one arid corner of Paldea, there have been
reports of a mysterious life-form. It’s said to
resemble a Donphan at first glance, albeit one
with gigantic tusks, tough scales, and an
aggressive disposition.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_01_03a

entries.text:
Leading theories hold that this being is nothing
less than a living relic of the dinosaur era, but
no one can say for sure. Apparently, it’s called
Great Tusk after the name of a strange being that
was written about in the mysterious Scarlet Book.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_01_04a

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #09\nIron Treads: An Alien Weapon?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_01_02b

entries.text:
In one arid corner of Paldea, there have been
reports of a mysterious life-form. It’s said to
resemble a Donphan at first glance, albeit one
that can abruptly assume a spherical shape and
launch into a swift rolling attack.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_01_03b

entries.text:
Rumors say this being is some kind of weapon
using technology not of this world, but no one
can say for sure. Apparently, it’s called Iron
Treads after the name of a strange being that was
written about in the mysterious Violet Book.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_01_04b

entries.text: There’s a magazine entitled “Occulture.” It’s the\nOctober issue. Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_02_01

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #10\nScream Tail: A Billion-Year-Old Jigglypuff?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_02_02a

entries.text:
Somewhere in a Paldean forest, it’s said, lurks
Scream Tail—a being with Jigglypuff’s own
endearing puffball appearance but also a
ferocious aggression that leads it to attack
anyone who comes near.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_02_03a

entries.text:
Its primitive appearance and savage nature have
prompted rumors that it could be a Jigglypuff
from one billion years ago. It’s named after a
creature in the Scarlet Book that is described as
having a distinctive tail and scream.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_02_04a

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #10\nIron Bundle: An Ancient Civilization’s Robot?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_02_02b

entries.text:
The mysterious Violet Book makes reference to a
being called Iron Bundle, which was said to look
like Delibird and to possess a spherical apparatus
from which it would fire huge blasts of ice to
propel itself through snowy lands.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_02_03b

entries.text:
Plenty of theories about it have been floated. A
leading one suggests it is the product of a long-
gone civilization—a notion supported by ancient
writings that describe the design and usage of
machines resembling Iron Bundle.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_02_04b

entries.text: There’s a magazine entitled “Occulture.” It’s the\nAugust issue. Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_03_01

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #08\nSlither Wing: A Prehistoric Volcarona, Revived?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_03_02a

entries.text:
There have been precious few sightings reported
of the ultra-mysterious Slither Wing, a being
whose name is taken from that of a similar-
seeming creature described in the ever-puzzling
Scarlet Book.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_03_03a

entries.text:
Slither Wing shares traits with Volcarona, so some
theorize that it may have been revived from
fossils from a prehistoric era that we have
discussed in these pages. However, no Volcarona
fossils of that era are known to have been found.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_03_04a

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #08\nIron Moth: A UFO Sent to Spy on Humankind?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_03_02b

entries.text:
The name Iron Moth was borrowed from that of a
flying object described in the era-defining Violet
Book. It was said to resemble Volcarona and
would descend from the skies, following people
around and occasionally even attacking them.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_03_03b

entries.text:
Some point to Iron Moth’s aggression as a sign
that it is, in fact, a UFO of sorts being controlled
by alien life. Perhaps something out there is using
Iron Moth to observe us, waiting for the moment
to mount an invasion...
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_03_04b

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #07\nSandy Shocks: A Magneton with a 10-Thousand-\nYear Lifespan?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_04_02a

entries.text:
Some scientists claim that this mysterious being is
a Magneton that has lived for 10 thousand years.
It has been sighted numerous times in Paldea’s
more arid regions, but there are no reports of it
ever having been caught.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_04_03a

entries.text:
It’s said that Sandy Shocks is an aggressive sort
and that some people who’ve seen it have been
attacked as well. It takes its name from a beast
with a matching description in the era-defining
Scarlet Book.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_04_04a

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #07\nIron Jugulis: Pokémon or Machine?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_04_02b

entries.text:
This flying life-form bearing a resemblance to
Hydreigon has been seen in a certain corner of
Paldea. It was reported to have razed an entire
building with a high-energy blast, then flown off
as if to find its next objective.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_04_03b

entries.text:
Iron Jugulis is theorized to be a sort of machine-
Hydreigon hybrid, as it combines the former’s
ruthlessness with the latter’s ferocity. It takes
its name from a similarly described entity in
the Violet Book.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_04_04b

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #06\nBrute Bonnet: Amoonguss Meets Dinosaur?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_05_02a

entries.text:
This bizarre creature is said to combine traits of
dinosaurs with those of the Pokémon Amoonguss.
It’s named after a fierce mushroom creature of
matching description that appears in the
renowned Scarlet Book.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_05_03a

entries.text:
Brute Bonnet certainly resembles Amoonguss,
though with its own unique twists: its gigantic
stature and seemingly low intelligence combine
to make it a savage, powerful fighter.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_05_04a

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #06\nIron Thorns: A Tyranitar of the Distant Future?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_05_02b

entries.text:
A strange being called Iron Thorns has been
sighted in a certain cave in Paldea. This being
bears a strong resemblance to Tyranitar, but it
apparently displays great coolheadedness and
prefers to avoid unnecessary fights.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_05_03b

entries.text:
It appears to be highly intelligent and clad in
metallic armor, causing some to speculate that it
may be a Tyranitar as it would appear a billion
years from now. Its name comes from a similarly
described entity that appears in the Violet Book.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_05_04b

entries.text: There’s a magazine entitled “Occulture.” It’s the\nMay issue. Do you want to read it?
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_06_01

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #05\nFlutter Mane: A Ghostly Pterosaur?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_06_02a

entries.text:
Flutter Mane—a name taken from a strange
creature with a matching description appearing in
the Scarlet Book—is said to float around the sky
at night with its long hair writhing about it.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_06_03a

entries.text:
Eyewitness accounts describe it as resembling a
giant Misdreavus at first glance, albeit a highly
fierce and aggressive one. Some believe that it’s
a ghost of a pterosaur from a long-gone era.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_06_04a

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #05\nIron Hands: Secretly a Cyborg?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_06_02b

entries.text:
This being’s name comes from the one given to
an iron-handed entity in the mysterious Violet
Book. It is said to have fists that move
independent of its body and to be capable of
throwing large, fast-moving vehicles.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_06_03b

entries.text:
A leading theory holds that Iron Hands was once
an athlete who became mortally wounded but
was kept alive by being made into a cyborg.
Why it so strongly resembles Hariyama, however,
remains unanswered.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_06_04b

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #04\nRoaring Moon: A Primeval Salamence?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_07_02a

entries.text:
This elusive creature is called Roaring Moon after
a similarly described being in the Scarlet Book. It
looks similar to Salamence when they undergo a
certain phenomenon elsewhere in the world, but
it’s unclear if there is any connection.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_07_03a

entries.text:
This creature scatters feathers as it flies around at
high speeds seeking prey. It’s thought to be more
savage than Salamence, and if you should
encounter one, it’s imperative that you avoid
actual contact.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_07_04a

entries.text: Enigmas of Paldea, File #04\nIron Valiant: An Experiment Gone Wrong?!
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_07_02b

entries.text:
This oddity’s name is borrowed from that of an
object described in the Violet Book. One theory
holds that it is in fact a robot—the product of a
mad scientist’s efforts to create the most
powerful psychic Pokémon of all.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_07_03b

entries.text:
According to its few eyewitnesses, Iron Valiant
appears similar to both Gardevoir and Gallade.
It’s also said to be cruel enough to take its
brilliantly shining blade and cut down anyone
confronting it without hesitation.
entries.label: a_sch_entrance01_ocalture_07_04b

phenomenon—which I’ve dubbed “Terastallizing.”

entries.text:
Thanks to my prototype Tera Orb, I secured
corporate funding for my research and made
a laboratory in the lighthouse near Cabo Poco.\c
Someday, though, I’ll return to the crater and
resume my study of these crystals.

entries.text:
At last I can resume work on the Tera Project!\c
I’ll move my research to the Zero Lab this month.
My team will be smaller, but no matter.\c
The strong influence of the crystals makes our
experiments much more unstable.
entries.label: a_w23_i12_01

entries.text:
The crystals’ power is tremendous! Their unstable
output made our corporate backers fret, but...\c
If we can harness this energy, it will open up
research possibilities we’d only dreamed of.\c
At last, paradise will be ours to create.
entries.label: a_w23_i12_02

entries.text:
Our time machine research has yielded a
triumph—a Pokémon from the ancient past!\c
I’ve named it Koraidon.\c
I was expecting one new life to treasure, but
what fortune to be blessed with this gift as well!

I’ve successfully brought more and more ancient
Pokémon to our time since the first one.\c

the book—a paradise where we three can live
happily together forever. I must make it real.

The Infernal Pass is subject to a relentless spew of
volcanic gas spit up from under its rocky terrain.\c
While this area has famously been used as a
training ground for years, visitors be warned:
you’d do best not to let the ogre find you here!

entries.text:
Long ago, the Crystal Pool was infused with
crystalline material from an unknown source.\c
Its water has a faint glow, but it’s safe to drink
and even serves as the village’s water source.\c
Tales say that gazing upon the glowing water can
allow you to meet those who have passed on.
entries.label: su1_spot_kanban_02

entries.text:
The two rivers that flow from Oni Mountain
converge here, at the Mossfell Confluence.\c
People say that items lost upriver eventually
wash up all the way down here.
entries.label: su1_spot_kanban_03

entries.text:
Taking a drink from the waters of Wisteria Pond
is said to grant eternal life.\c
Though it is nutritious and quite famed, please
be sure to boil the water before consumption.
entries.label: su1_spot_kanban_04

entries.text:
The large, pointed rock spire jutting out from
the lake ahead is called the Fallen Horn.\c
It’s believed that long ago, this giant rock was
actually one of the horns atop Oni Mountain.\c
When the horn fell, its tip broke off. This part
of the horn is now enshrined at Kitakami Hall.
entries.label: su1_spot_kanban_05

entries.text:
Only a select few know of this power spot...
The Gracious Stones!\c
Curiously, no grass grows within their ring.
Curiouser yet, gazing upon them lifts the spirits!

entries.text:
“The Mossened Boulder”\c
It’s said that long ago, this mass of rock fell from
the sky into Mossui Town.\c
It was feared that the ogre on the mountain threw
the boulder to wreak havoc on the village.\c
But it is now understood to be a fragment of the
Fallen Horn, one of the Six Wonders of Kitakami.

entries.text:
“Loyal Three Monument”\c
Long ago, these three courageous Pokémon
protected Mossui Town from destruction.\c
They defeated the ogre that had come to
attack the village, at the cost of their own lives.\c
Their remains were laid to rest with the
people’s respects below these very statues.

I am calling the area found below Area Zero the
[VAR 0xFF00(0006)]Area Zero Underdepths[VAR 0xFF00(0000)]. From the composition
of the rock, I would date the cavern’s formation
to two million years ago. There are indications
that many objects—or creatures perhaps—filled
the space prior to the current cavern’s formation.
entries.label: su2_bg_zerocave_bg_02_01a

entries.text:
The depths bottom out approximately 3,300
feet beneath the surface. There are indications
of numerous past cave-ins, likely resulting from
tectonic activity and erosion caused by rainwater
or groundwater, but it appears that the ground
has remained stable since the last major cave-in.
